entries.caption:
if your plan always falls apart around week five, that's not you failing. that's the part everyone hits.

the results run behind the work. for a stretch you do everything right and the mirror says nothing back. that's the valley, and it's exactly where most men quit.

count the streak, not the mirror. if you're still showing up at week six it starts to show.

week five isn't proof it doesn't work. it's the test.

comment "build" for the guide.

sat across a coach charging 500 pounds a month and thought i was behind. took me a while to get it wasn't the app, it was what i built around mine.

follow me, i'm posting what i built after that call.

went back to london for six months. first time was survival. this time, museums, mornings, calls from cafes. closing a door doesn't mean you hated the room.

follow me for how a city stops owning you.

hit every goal i set for my 20s and it made it worse. the business took off, the ambitions went up faster than the wins did.

follow me for the part nobody shows you after the win.

a bad season isn't low motivation. it's still cooking with what you had, still showing up to an ugly park, still asking out loud if it's worth it.

follow me for what i changed the season after.

19, still training in a garage nobody in my family took seriously. 23, moved out alone, no help. 24, london for six months and couldn't close a single sale. 25, barcelona, first month over ten thousand.

follow me, i'm posting the years in between.

a saturday training a client while my girlfriend built her own day taught me more than most weeks do. you don't get a life you want by accident.

follow me, i post the real week, not the highlight.

one friend from home still calls me every single week. different time zone, same hour. the friends who last aren't the ones nearby.

follow me, i talk more about what keeps people close.

trained alone in a garage for two years before anyone noticed. nobody claps for the first two years. that's exactly why they count.

follow me, i'm posting the other 4 signs this week.

a client flew in and we met in person for the first time. i thought the milestone would be a number. it was someone trusting me enough to book a flight.

follow me for more of the part that doesn't make the highlight reel.

two hours a day standing on a train never built anyone's life. quit on a phone call and walked out crying. not sad, relieved.

follow me for what i built instead of that train.

my mother asked if i really thought i'd make it doing this. i didn't argue back. i just stopped explaining and kept training.

follow me, there's 4 more moments like this one.

every year i told myself this time is different. quit after two weeks, blamed the schedule. quit after a month, blamed the program. the thing that finally worked wasn't more willpower.

follow me for the system that ended the cycle.

thought i needed 2 hours to make training count. the plan i was following assumed i had no job. cut it to 45 minutes, four days a week. more progress in fewer sessions.

follow me for how less training time actually worked.

trained six days a week and wondered why nothing changed. more sessions, less sleep, no actual recovery. cut to four days, added recovery, results showed up in weeks.

follow me, i post the plans that actually work.

you feel guilty for missing a session because you have one to miss. you feel behind because you're still measuring yourself. guilt means you still care, that's what gets you through.

follow me for less guilt, more of an actual plan.

two strangers stopped us on the street and asked if i was happy. i didn't even know how to answer. i realized i hadn't asked myself that since i left argentina.

follow me, more of what that month taught me.

nobody in my family is religious. this month i bought a bible anyway. i read a few pages every night, testing if an old book actually has anything to say. taking notes like it's any other book i study.

follow me, i talk more about what i'm learning.

10/10 confident when i started yet another program alone. 7/10 by week three, same plan, no adjustments. 3/10 by week five, plateaued, nobody noticed. back to 10/10 the week someone actually looked at my training.

follow me, you don't need another program, you need eyes on it.

things that are normal when you train alone with no one watching. you guess if the form was right. you repeat the same mistake for months without knowing. you plateau and blame genetics, not the missing feedback.

follow me for the corrections nobody's giving you solo.

what's actually stopping you from starting today? not the gym. not the time.

follow me, i'll tell you what it actually is.

"isn't 30 a bit late to start this seriously?" me, training anyway at 26.

follow me, there's no age where this stops working.

the weekend picks your monday whether you like it or not. friday drinks, saturday regret, sunday write-off. or friday early, saturday trained, sunday actually rested.

follow me for the version of the weekend that works.

a client with four jobs taught me something about excuses. he said there was no time for a real plan. we built one around his actual schedule, not an ideal one. now the plan bends, he doesn't.

follow me, there's a pt 2 to this.

6am, training before anyone needs anything from me. 10am, a call with a client in a different time zone. 1pm, cooking the only meal i actually control that day. 11pm, same thing tomorrow.

follow me, this is the real day, not the highlight.

5 signs you stopped asking if you're actually happy. you chase the next city instead of the next year. stillness feels like falling behind. you can't remember the last real question you asked yourself.

follow me, i'm posting what changed for me.

people think i'm calm because nothing ever went wrong for me. 19 in a garage while people laughed at the skinny kid. 24 in a season with no sun and a business barely alive. the calm isn't luck, it's what's left after all that.

follow me, i post the seasons, not just the result.

the hard years weren't bad luck. they were the toll.

follow me for what that toll bought.

you complain about the gym being loud because you have one. sore legs because they still work. early calls because clients trust you with them. some of this you once just wanted.

follow me, i keep count of the things i almost missed.

i started looking at people like i was watching from outside. not taking it personal when someone acts a certain way. some people are just going to be who they are.

follow me, i post more of how i think now.

i was their 10/10 son until i said no for the first time. 8/10 when i quit the safe plan. 6/10 when i moved countries without their blessing. 1/10 when i built a life they never approved of.

follow me, you don't need a perfect score from anyone.

i told my parents and my sister something i never had before. that i'd started reading the bible, on my own. a version of me they hadn't met yet.

follow me, i'm still figuring this out.

things that are normal as an online coach nobody tells you. some weeks you coach better than you train. a client's win carries you further than your own pr. you still doubt a plan you've run a hundred times.

follow me, i don't only post the clean version.

i hadn't asked myself a real question in about two years. the adrenaline of the new does that to you.

follow me, there's more to this.

who are you really doing this for? not the mirror. not the ones who doubted you first.

follow me, i still ask myself this every week.

some things you build quietly, alone. one piece at a time, nobody watching.

follow me, i post the parts nobody sees getting built.

"why do you always train right at sunset?" me, ignoring the question. and training anyway.

follow me, some habits don't need a good reason.

i used to think the hard years were just bad luck. now i think they were the price for something i couldn't see yet.

follow me, i post the seasons, not just the result.

saturday plans, picked by whatever life throws first. a client texts at 8am. training, because the body doesn't take saturdays off. somehow that's still the plan i wanted.

follow me for more of the saturdays that don't go as planned.

two women stopped us to share something they didn't have to. complete strangers, a question that went deep fast. we told them things we hadn't said to people who know us.

follow me, that conversation stayed with me.

a lesson from my girlfriend that changed how i coach clients. she plans her whole day before she even leaves the house. i used to wing it and call it flexibility. now every client of mine starts with a real plan.

follow me, there's a pt 2 to this.

most men blame the hormone before they check the habits.

5 signs it was never your testosterone:

1. you wake up already tired and that is a sleep quality problem, not a hormone one 2. you dread starting, not the actual work, that is dopamine not drive 3. you cannot begin anything without coffee so the caffeine is running your mornings 4. you crash hard at 3pm which is what a big rushed lunch does to anyone 5. eight hours in bed still feels like six because of late screens and no wind down

fix the inputs for six weeks before you pay for a test.

comment "build" and i will send you the full breakdown

not for my health. my friends were not going anywhere and i knew it.

lost most of them anyway and that part i did not plan for.

but mondays stopped being a write off and the gym stopped feeling like something i owed the weekend.

everyone asks what i added. nothing. i just stopped paying for two bad days every seven.

agree or not. comment "build" for the guide

"train six days a week or you are not serious." i said it for years.

six days was me not trusting that three could be enough so i covered the doubt with volume.

added weight, dropped to three real sessions, got stronger and slept better.

it was never a discipline problem, it was a trust problem.

agree or not. comment "build" for the guide

motivation shows up twice a month. the men around you show up every day, or they don't and you quietly match them.

you don't rise to your goals, you fall to your circle.

look at the three men you text most, that is your next year.

agree or not. comment "build"

it is not your metabolism. it is keeping your 20s habits into your 30s and calling it blowing off steam.

the body keeps the receipts, the late nights and the weekend reset that bleeds into sunday and the start monday that has been fourteen mondays.

nothing aged you. you just never updated the routine.

agree or not. comment "build" for the guide

"you can go out with the boys and still stay in shape." sure. for about two years.

then the hangover costs two days instead of one and you spend the week undoing two nights.

i stopped at 18 and the gym stopped feeling like a punishment almost right away.

the pub will still be open at 40. your 30s won't.

agree or not. comment "build"

so does everyone past a certain age. yours works fine when the food is real and you move before you sit down for nine hours.

it was never slow, it was unmeasured. you have no real idea what you eat in a week.

track it honestly for seven days before you blame your body.

agree or not. comment "build" for the guide

four exercises, none of them hard. a phone in one hand between sets. an hour spent and nothing moved.

busy is comfortable, progress is not.

you can train for a full hour and completely avoid the work.

too harsh? agree or not. comment "build"

sparta did not run on willpower, it ran on how the men were raised. the environment did the work.

put the gym clothes on the chair, not folded in the drawer. charge the phone in another room. keep the real food at eye level.

willpower is what is left after you remove the friction. it is the result, not the trick.

agree or not. comment "build" for the guide

the long hours, the job, the years of training with no one correcting your form. none of that was in your hands.

the next six weeks are.

what happened is not your fault. what happens now is, and that is the good news.

comment "build" and i will send you the plan

you are on time for everything. you hit deadlines. you would never leave a client hanging.

5 signs you are disciplined everywhere except your body:

1. you plan your work week to the hour and improvise every meal 2. you would never skip a meeting but the gym is if there is time 3. you research a work decision for days and train off whatever you saw last 4. you show up for everyone and the one hour for yourself is first to go 5. you call it a busy season and it has been three years

the discipline is already there. it is just pointed everywhere else.

comment "build" for the guide

you can start at 33. with twenty minutes. flat and tired. with no one watching.

you just can't start tomorrow again, that is the one version that never works.

a client told me restarting is harder than starting. she was right and she still restarted, that is the whole skill.

which line is you? comment "build"

i trained a man worth more than i will say here for two years. he never asked what something cost. he asked what waiting would cost him.

3 things he taught me about staying in shape:

1. decisions get measured in time, not money, a skipped session costs a week not an hour 2. treat the body like an asset with compounding returns, small deposits and never zero 3. there is no gift and no secret, he just spent his hours like they counted

it was never talent. it was the time.

comment "build" for the guide

you will rebuild your entire week for a two day work trip. flights, hotel, meetings to the minute.

but not for the one hour a day that keeps you sane.

the calendar always finds room for everyone else. you plan around your body, you never plan for it.

sound familiar? comment "build"

you think it is your genetics. you think you have tried everything.

it was neither. it was a plan built for a life you do not have, five sessions an hour each with no travel and no night shift and no kids.

the plan fit someone else. get one that fits you.

comment "build" for the guide

at 19 i trained in the garage at 8pm, the one hour nobody walked past. the pull up bar came four months later, when my dad finally saw i meant it.

at 26 a client flew across the world to train with me. we did dips, drank mate, laughed on the beach.

same guy. same closed doors. they just open the other way now.

comment "build" if you train alone

clean plate, better energy. clean training, better sleep. clean mornings, better decisions. clean circle, better years.

you do not need more supplements or more sessions or more rules. you need less noise.

pick the line above that is the messiest for you and fix that one first.

comment "build" for the guide

your plan did not fail. it assumed a life you do not live.

five sessions an hour each with no travel. yours has to survive a double shift and a kid with a fever.

the fix is a plan that fits, not more willpower.

comment "build" for the guide

you will run a stranger's plan for a year. take the supplement the label picks for you. trust a map for a road you have never driven.

but you will not back your own plan for six weeks before you decide it does not work.

give yourself the six weeks you would give a stranger.

comment "build" for the guide

you are not a beginner. you train hard. and you have been at the same level for a year.

you do not need a transformation. you need one thing corrected.

a client of mine trained for years and felt his back for the first time after one grip cue. that was it. one thing.

film one set from the side and send it to someone who knows. fixing one beats adding five.

comment "build" for the guide

focus is not something you install. it is what is left when you stop grabbing the phone every time there is a gap. i gave my hands something else to do. that was the whole fix.

comment "RESET"

the bathroom is the last place you are truly alone and most people fill it with noise anyway. i turned it into the one moment a day i train my brain instead of feeding it.

comment "RESET" for the guide

i didn't delete instagram or set screen limits. i just got bored of it. when your brain has something better to reach for, the scroll stops holding you on its own.

comment "RESET"

the point is not to think deep thoughts. it is to be okay doing nothing for a few minutes without reaching for something. i practice it where no one is watching, every single day.

comment "RESET" for the guide
